name: Elite Yeti
usage: Read this file before choosing character states or animation clip names.
Animation name is the exact physical clip key. display_name and source_name describe it; aliases are semantic role hints only.

Resolve the exact stateFolder and clipName with the resolver this file exports — resolveCharacterAnimation(manifest, candidates, { state?, direction? }), or selectCharacterState(...) where that is what it exports.
Prefer an exact user-requested display name or clip name before generic roles such as idle, walk, run, jump, or attack.
CharacterAgent resolves idle, movement, and attack clips across the full manifest and switches state folders automatically.
Rotations are static poses only. Use animator.setPose(...) or characterRotationFrameName(...) for a deliberate static pose; setClip('idle', ...) always means a real animated idle clip.
resolveCharacterAnimation(...) and chooseClip(...) return undefined when no clip matches. Handle that explicitly; never silently replace a missing animation with rotations.
For simple roaming/walking NPCs, use CharacterAgent instead of custom straight-line movement. Its built-in roaming picks walkable targets and follows A* paths around blockers.

For autonomous movement, update movement/pathing before choosing the animation direction. Direction should come from actual movement after collision/sliding, not only the intended path target. Do not cache a facing direction before followPath/collision movement and reuse it for setClip.
If using setDirection as a temporary facing lock, do not call it again after releasing movement/facing control in the same update branch.
CharacterAgent owns the visible sprite as agent.sprite. Do not create a separate scene.add.sprite for the same character.
Keep each character controller or agent in the scene update loop for any movement or animation changes.
When adding behavior to a specific NPC, use explicit references or agent.role/agent.id. Do not infer identity from array position or agent.atlasKey.includes(name); atlas keys are UUID-based.
For dialogue portraits, use states[].portrait.path when present. Build the URL with characterAssetUrl(characterId, path) from the runtime helper.
For portrait lip-sync/vocal animation, use states[].vocal_animation.path when present. It is a grid with moods as rows and visemes as columns.
Use SpriteAnimator(sprite, atlasKey, animations, stateFolder) and animator.setClip(clipName, direction, stateFolder) for resolved clips.
